Thanks Mark — draft answers below based on product & infra guidance. Mark / Ben please flag anything I should change before we send. I'm pasting Jenna's questions inline to keep context.

-----
On Tue, Sep 21, 2026 at 08:42 Jenna Cole <jenna.cole@everledger.com> wrote:
> 1) Can requests (prompts + metadata) be guaranteed to stay within a single cloud region?

Draft answer: Yes — Redwood Hosted API routes and stores customer request data in a single region by default when the customer selects a region-lock option. For customers that opt in to region-lock, all processing, short-lived caches (KV/prefix caches), and primary logs are kept within the selected region (we currently support us-east-1 and eu-west-1 as region-lock options). We do not replicate primary request data cross-region unless the customer opts into cross-region redundancy.

> 2) What is the default retention for request logs, diagnostics, and backups?

Draft answer: Default system retention (Hosted API): request logs: 30 days; diagnostic traces (if enabled): 90 days; ephemeral KV/prefix caches: seconds-to-hours (evicted automatically); automated snapshot backups: 30 days. Customers can request shorter retention windows for their account via support. Audit logs (control plane events) are retained 365 days for customers on enterprise plans.

> 3) If we request a tenant-level erase, what parts of the system are purged and how long does full eradication take?

Draft answer: Erasure process (Hosted API): 1) Submit a data-erase support ticket with the account id and the scope (prompts, embeddings, logs). 2) Within 4 hours we mark all primary customer objects for deletion and remove access from live indices and caches. 3) Propagation and background cleanup (object storage, logs, and model-served caches) complete within 14 days in normal cases. 4) Snapshot and backup purges complete within 30 days; we provide a deletion attestation when the process finishes. For urgent or regulatory cases we can accelerate the timeline under an SLA.

> 4) Do you ever use customer data to improve models?

Draft answer: By default, Redwood does not use customer-provided prompts or outputs to train or fine-tune public models. Model training on customer data requires an explicit opt-in setting ("Diagnostics & Training") and a contractual agreement. Aggregated service telemetry (anonymized, low-cardinality metrics about latencies and error rates) may be used to improve the platform.

Hi Jenna,

Thanks for the Q; please find our completed responses below (I've attached the filled spreadsheet and a high-level dataflow diagram for your team). If you want this in an attestation PDF we can generate that after you confirm acceptance of the timelines.

Attached: everledger_security_qna_v3_filled.xlsx, redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf, hostedapi-retention-summary.csv

Redwood responses (summary):
- Region-lock: Yes. For customers that select region-lock we keep request processing, ephemeral caches, and primary logs in the chosen region (we support us-east-1 and eu-west-1). No cross-region replication unless explicitly requested.
- Retention defaults: request logs 30 days; diagnostic traces (opt-in) 90 days; ephemeral KV/prefix caches: automatically evicted (seconds→hours); automated snapshot backups: 30 days; control-plane audit logs (enterprise): 365 days. Customers may request shorter windows.
- Erasure process & timeline: submit a data-erase ticket → mark-for-deletion within 4 hours → live indices & caches removed within 4 hours → background object/store cleanup completes within 14 days → snapshot/backup purge completes within 30 days. We provide a signed attestation when purge completes. For high-priority regulatory requests we can accelerate under an SLA.
- Model training: Redwood does not use customer prompts/outputs to train models by default. Training on customer data requires explicit opt-in and contract terms. Platform telemetry (anonymized) may be used to improve service reliability.
- Encryption & keys: All data in transit uses TLS 1.2+; at-rest storage is encrypted with AES-256. Customer-managed KMS integration is available for Dedicated/Private customers and as an optional add-on for Hosted with enterprise contract.

Next steps: please confirm if Everledger would like us to: (a) produce a signed attestation PDF, (b) shorten any retention windows, or (c) enable region-lock for a test tenant so you can validate data residency.

Happy to hop on a short call if useful.

Regards,
